newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 14.33 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 14.33 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell two basis points to 14.33 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 50 billion bolivars of 177-day "monetary stabilization" notes, or TEM, bills with a 14.35 percent coupon for a price of 100.01 pct. At last week's auction six month notes yielded 14.35 percent

The bank also sold ten billion bolivars of 267-day notes with a 14.61 percent coupon at a price of 98.82 percent, and ten billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 14.87 percent coupon at an average price of 98.05 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 203 basis points to 16.40 percent for the 269-day bills, and 248 basis points to 17.17 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
